headline: A new company called SignSplit has launched with a $400 million funding round from the technology group W Group to let people get paid when AI developers use their data, voice or likeness.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 5: a large launch round for a consent-and-payment data service, but the figures come from the company's own announcement.
importance_line: What changed is that a newly launched, heavily funded start-up offers a way to attach consent and payment to personal data used for AI, which matters to people and creators whose work AI models use, then to AI developers who want data with clear permission, then to W Group, which is backing it, and the doubt is that the figures come from the company's own announcement, part of the support is not cash and no AI developer is named as a customer.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports, from the company's announcement, that SignSplit, a company founded in 2024 that lets people digitally sign their data, voice, likeness or other work to set the terms on which AI developers may use it, has launched with a $400 million “strategic seed round” from W Group, a group of 11 financial technology businesses, at a valuation of $1 billion. The company's release says the financing combines money with a multi-year package of other support from W Group, and contributors can also place data in shared “data pools” for AI developers, with payment according to how often it is used.
notes: Full SiliconANGLE article read, and the company's own release on PR Newswire (5 Oct 2026), which is the primary source. SiliconANGLE spells the name inconsistently (SignSplit, SplitSign, SignedSplit); 'SignSplit' is used as in the release. Amount and valuation are the company's own figures.
